newsitem.title: JAPAN: GE chairman urges Japan firms to cut weak units.
newsitem.headline: GE chairman urges Japan firms to cut weak units.

text.p: The chairman of General Electric admonished Japanese corporate managers Wednesday for being reluctant to sell off weak and unpromising subsidiaries.

Speaking at the 50th anniversary of the Kansai Association of Corporate Executives in Osaka, the commercial hub of western Japan, the chairman, John Welch, also suggested that Japanese managers speed up their decisions.

"Americans tend to think in terms of weeks and months, while Japanese take years and decades," Welch said in his address. "Patience was good for much of the 70s and early 80s but in the 90s, things have changed."
He said Japan's virtue for patience and paternalism had now become an impediment, and urged managers to discard the notion of disloyalty to their employees when detaching weak subsidiaries.

"It may be time for Japan to consider looking into its traditional business practices and to start rationalising -- selling off smaller and weaker business or perhaps even merging them with stronger ones," Welch said.
"Selling weaker businesses is not betraying the employees," Welch said.
"Forming subsidiaries and putting them to sleep in corners makes no sense," Welch said. "It is the manager's job to create an atmosphere where every employee is happy."
Many Japanese managers responded to Welch's comments by saying Japan's system of lifetime employment posed different problems.
